blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Connect n8n to GoHighLevel for free, unlimited self-hosted automation. Webhook triggers, API nodes, and four real GHL workflows you can build today.
blogPosts.content:
Zapier costs money at scale, and Make hits execution limits fast. When you need unlimited runs, full control over your data, and zero per-task fees, n8n is the answer — an open-source workflow tool you can self-host for free. At GHL Prime we use n8n for complex client builds that would cost hundreds of dollars a month on Zapier. This guide covers connecting n8n to GoHighLevel, the core nodes you need, and four real workflows you can deploy today.

n8n vs Zapier vs Make — Which Should You Use?

All three tools connect apps and automate workflows, but they sit at very different points on the cost and control spectrum. Here is how they compare for a GoHighLevel agency.

Factorn8nZapierMake
CostFree (self-hosted)From $20/moFrom $9/mo
Task limitsUnlimitedLimitedLimited
Self-hostableYesNoNo
Learning curveMediumEasyEasy-Medium
Best forAgencies, devs, high volumeSimple zaps, non-technical usersMid-complexity automations

The verdict: reach for Zapier when you need a quick, simple automation and do not want to touch a server. Choose n8n when you are running high volume, building complex multi-step logic, or handling data you would rather keep on your own infrastructure. For most agencies scaling past a handful of clients, n8n pays for itself almost immediately.

Setting Up n8n (Two Options)

You have two ways to get an n8n instance running. Pick based on whether you want zero maintenance or zero cost.

Option A — n8n Cloud. Sign up at n8n.io/cloud and you get a managed instance with no server to maintain. Plans start from around $20/mo and include unlimited executions, which is still a flat fee rather than per-task pricing. This is the fastest path if you would rather not manage infrastructure.

Option B — Self-hosted on a VPS (free software). Spin up a small server — a $6 DigitalOcean droplet is plenty to start — and run n8n in Docker. The software itself is free, so your only cost is the server. Run this command to get going:

docker run -it --rm --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -v ~/.n8n:/home/node/.n8n n8nio/n8n

Once it is running, access the editor at http://your-server-ip:5678. That command is perfect for testing, but for production you will want to put nginx in front with SSL so traffic is encrypted and you can use a proper domain.

Connecting n8n to GoHighLevel

There are two reliable ways to wire n8n and GHL together, and most real builds use both.

Method 1 — GHL Webhook to n8n Webhook Trigger. This is how you push events from GHL into n8n in real time:

  1. In n8n, add a Webhook node and copy its production URL.
  2. In your GHL Workflow, Add Action → Webhook and set it to POST to the n8n URL.
  3. Send a test from GHL so n8n captures the payload structure.
  4. Reference the incoming fields in downstream nodes.

Method 2 — n8n HTTP Request node to the GHL API. This is how n8n reads or writes data back into GHL. The base URL is https://services.leadconnectorhq.com, and you authenticate with a Bearer token from GHL Settings > API Keys. Common endpoints:

  • GET /contacts and POST /contacts — read and create contacts
  • PUT /contacts/{id} — update a contact
  • POST /contacts/{id}/tags — add tags to a contact

n8n Workflow 1 — GHL New Contact to AI Enrichment to Update Contact

Turn a bare email address into a fully enriched contact record automatically.

  1. Webhook trigger fires when a new contact is created in GHL.
  2. HTTP Request node calls an enrichment service like Clearbit or Hunter.io with the contact email.
  3. IF node checks whether a company was found — if yes, continue; if no, skip enrichment.
  4. HTTP Request sends a PUT /contacts/{id} back to GHL with company name, LinkedIn URL, and industry.
  5. POST /contacts/{id}/tags adds an enriched tag so your team knows the record is complete.

Now every new lead arrives with context, and your sales reps stop manually Googling prospects.

n8n Workflow 2 — GHL Pipeline Won to Invoice + Notification System

One pipeline-stage change kicks off your entire post-sale process — all from a single webhook, with zero Zapier tasks consumed.

  1. Webhook fires when a GHL opportunity moves to the Won stage.
  2. Stripe API node creates the invoice.
  3. DocuSign API node sends the contract for signature.
  4. Slack node notifies the #sales channel of the new win.
  5. Gmail node sends the client a welcome email.
  6. GHL API moves the contact to your Onboarding pipeline and adds a won-client tag.

This is the kind of multi-platform chain that would burn through a Zapier task quota in days. On self-hosted n8n it runs unlimited at no per-task cost.

n8n Workflow 3 — Scheduled GHL Data Backup to Google Sheets

GoHighLevel does not auto-export your contacts, so a scheduled backup protects you from data loss and account issues.

  1. Cron node triggers every Sunday at midnight.
  2. GHL API calls GET /contacts and paginates through every record.
  3. Google Sheets node clears the backup sheet.
  4. The workflow writes all contacts into the sheet.
  5. Gmail node sends a "Backup complete — X contacts" confirmation.

A simple weekly snapshot means you are never one accidental deletion away from disaster.

n8n Workflow 4 — AI-Powered GHL Message Classifier

Route every inbound message intelligently using AI instead of manual triage.

  1. Webhook fires on every new inbound message in GHL.
  2. OpenAI node classifies the intent: booking request, complaint, general, or unsubscribe.
  3. Switch node routes based on the classification:
    • Booking: add a GHL tag and create a task for the team.
    • Complaint: fire an urgent Slack alert.
    • Unsubscribe: apply the GHL DND tag and remove the contact from active sequences.
    • General: start your standard response workflow.

Your inbox effectively triages itself, and nothing urgent slips through the cracks.

Tips for Running n8n in Production

Once you move past testing, treat your n8n instance like the critical infrastructure it is:

  • Always use HTTPS — never run a production webhook endpoint over plain HTTP.
  • Enable basic auth on your instance so the editor is not publicly accessible.
  • Set up the built-in error workflow to alert you the moment any automation fails.
  • Keep n8n updated to get security patches and new nodes.
  • Store your GHL API key as an n8n Credential — never hardcode it into a node.

Follow those five rules and your automations stay secure, reliable, and easy to maintain as you scale.

blogPosts.content:
SimpleTalk is one of the leading AI voice agent platforms, and it integrates directly with GoHighLevel to power both inbound and outbound AI calling that qualifies leads, books appointments, and handles follow-ups automatically. At GHL Prime, we have deployed SimpleTalk AI agents across home services, real estate, and healthcare clients — and the results have been hard to ignore. This guide walks you through everything: connecting SimpleTalk to GoHighLevel, building your first agent, writing a conversation script that actually converts, and triggering outbound calls straight from your GHL workflows.

What Is SimpleTalk and How Does It Work With GHL?

SimpleTalk is an AI voice platform that makes and receives phone calls using natural, human-sounding voices. Instead of a clunky IVR menu, your contacts have a real conversation — and the AI knows how to qualify, book, and route based on what they say.

The integration loop with GoHighLevel is straightforward:

  1. A GHL workflow triggers SimpleTalk — either through the native action or a webhook.
  2. SimpleTalk calls the contact using your scripted agent.
  3. The call produces outcome data — answered, voicemail, qualified, or booked — which is sent back to GHL.
  4. GHL continues the automation based on that outcome: applying a tag, moving the contact in a pipeline, or firing an SMS.

That closed loop is what makes SimpleTalk GoHighLevel deployments so powerful — the AI does the talking, and GHL handles everything before and after.

SimpleTalk vs GHL Native Voice AI — Which Should You Use?

GoHighLevel now ships with its own Voice AI, so the obvious question is whether you even need SimpleTalk. Here is the honest breakdown.

FeatureGHL Native Voice AISimpleTalk
SetupBuilt in, simpleSeparate platform via integration/webhook
Inbound answeringYes (basic)Yes (full)
Outbound from workflowsNoYes
Conversation flow controlLimited customisationFull flow builder
Outcome data back to GHLMinimalRich (qualified, booked, voicemail, etc.)
Best forSmall/simple after-hours answeringAgencies, high volume, complex flows

Our verdict: use SimpleTalk for serious agency deployments where you need outbound calling, branching conversation logic, and detailed outcome tracking. Stick with GHL native Voice AI if all you need is simple after-hours call answering for a single small business.

Step 1 — Create Your SimpleTalk Account and Connect to GHL

  1. Sign up at simpletalk.ai and verify your account.
  2. Go to Integrations > GoHighLevel.
  3. Click connect and complete the OAuth authorize flow when GHL prompts you.
  4. Select the sub-account (location) you want SimpleTalk to operate in.
  5. Run a test connection to confirm the link is live before building anything.

Always connect at the sub-account level so each client stays isolated — a habit every GHL agency should keep.

Step 2 — Create Your First AI Agent in SimpleTalk

Inside SimpleTalk, click New Agent and configure the basics:

  • Name the agent (e.g. "Sarah — Inbound Receptionist").
  • Choose a natural voice — pick one that matches your brand and avoids the robotic feel.
  • Set the language and timezone so calls happen at the right local hours.
  • Select the agent type: Inbound (answers calls) or Outbound (places calls).
  • Assign a phone number for the agent to call from or receive on.

Step 3 — Write Your Agent's Conversation Script

SimpleTalk uses a visual flow builder made of conversation nodes. A reliable structure looks like this:

  • Opening node: "Hi, this is [Agent Name] calling from [Business Name]. Am I speaking with [First Name]?" — if yes, move to qualification; if no, apologise and end politely.
  • Qualification node (max 3 questions): the service needed, the area/location, and the timeline — within a week or two versus a future project.
  • Booking node: "I'd love to get you booked in with our team. Do you have a few minutes to pick a time?" — if yes, transfer or book; if no, send the booking link.
  • Fallback node: "No problem — let me have one of our team call you back within the hour."

Here is a sample home-services script we deploy for clients:

Opening: "Hi, this is Sarah from Apex Plumbing. Am I speaking with John?"

Qualify: "Great — what kind of plumbing issue are you dealing with? ... And which suburb are you in? ... Is this something you need sorted in the next week or two, or further down the track?"

Book: "Perfect, John. I'd love to get you booked in with one of our plumbers. Do you have a couple of minutes to pick a time that works?"

Fallback: "All good — I'll have one of our team give you a quick call back within the hour to lock it in."

Step 4 — Trigger SimpleTalk Calls from GHL Workflows

There are two ways to fire a SimpleTalk call from GoHighLevel.

Method 1 — Native action. In your GHL workflow, choose Add Action > SimpleTalk > Make Call, select the agent, and map the contact's phone number field. Done — no code required.

Method 2 — Webhook. Add a webhook action that sends a POST to your SimpleTalk webhook URL with the contact details:

POST https://api.simpletalk.ai/v1/calls
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "phone": "{{contact.phone}}",
  "name": "{{contact.first_name}}",
  "agent_id": "agt_8f2a9c41"
}

When to trigger calls:

  • New lead: call immediately while intent is hot.
  • Cold lead at 3 days: re-engagement call.
  • 24 hours before an appointment: a confirmation reminder.
  • 2 hours after service: a follow-up and review request.

Step 5 — Send Call Outcomes Back to GHL

This step is what separates a gimmick from a real system. Configure your SimpleTalk webhook to POST call results back into GHL and map each outcome to an action:

  • Answered + qualified: tag simpletalk-qualified and move the contact into the Qualified pipeline stage.
  • Not interested: tag the contact and remove them from active sequences.
  • Voicemail: tag voicemail-left and fire an SMS follow-up.
  • No answer: schedule an automatic callback in 2 hours.

With outcomes flowing back, your SimpleTalk GHL integration becomes a self-managing lead engine.

Real Results From SimpleTalk + GHL Deployments

  • Home services: 40% of inbound calls were qualified and booked entirely by the AI agent, no human touch.
  • Real estate: an outbound campaign to 300 cold leads hit an 18% answer rate and converted 11% into booked appointments.
  • Healthcare: after-hours coverage handled 100% of calls with zero missed — every patient reached a real conversation.

Common SimpleTalk Setup Mistakes

  • No fallback node — calls go silent when the contact says something unexpected. Always build the catch-all.
  • A robotic voice — pick a natural voice or hang-ups spike in the first ten seconds.
  • Not mapping outcomes back — without webhook results, GHL has no idea what happened on the call.
  • Wrong calling hours — set a sensible window like 9am to 7pm local time to avoid annoyed prospects and compliance issues.
  • Not A/B testing opening lines — small tweaks to the first sentence move answer and continuation rates more than anything else.

SimpleTalk Pricing — What to Expect

Pricing changes over time, so always check simpletalk.ai for current rates. Generally you can expect a per-minute call charge plus a platform fee. If you are running high volume, it is worth negotiating a custom plan — providers are usually flexible at scale. blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Use the GoHighLevel API to build custom integrations Zapier cannot. Auth, key endpoints, webhooks, real code examples, and when to hire a GHL developer.
blogPosts.content:
The GoHighLevel API reaches what Zapier and native integrations cannot. Push leads from a custom website form the instant they submit, pull live pipeline data into Power BI, sync a bespoke booking system, or route messages through a compliance-approved SMS provider. At GHL Prime we build custom GHL API integrations every week. This guide covers what the API can do, how authentication works, the endpoints you will use most, and four real-world integration patterns you can model from.

GHL API Basics — What You Need to Know

The GoHighLevel API is a standard REST API that speaks JSON. Every request goes to the base URL https://services.leadconnectorhq.com and is authenticated with a Bearer token — either an Agency key or a Location (sub-account) key, depending on the scope of what you are building.

  • Authentication: pass your token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY header on every request.
  • Rate limit: roughly 100 requests per 10 seconds per location. Build retry-with-backoff logic and batch where you can.
  • Versions: there is a v1 (older, legacy) and a v2 (current, recommended). Always build new GHL API integrations against v2.
  • Docs: the full reference lives at developers.gohighlevel.com.

Because it is plain REST and JSON, you can call it from any language or platform — Node.js, Python, PHP, a serverless function, or a no-code HTTP step inside a workflow.

Getting Your GHL API Key

There are two kinds of keys, and choosing the right one matters for both security and scope.

  • Agency key: in your agency dashboard go to Settings > Agency > API Keys > Create. This key can act across multiple sub-accounts.
  • Location key: open the specific sub-account, then go to Settings > API > Create. This key is scoped to that one client.

Use location keys for single-client integrations — they limit blast radius if a key ever leaks. Reserve the agency key for cross-account tooling that genuinely needs to touch many sub-accounts at once.

The 10 Most Used GHL API Endpoints

Nearly every integration we build leans on the same handful of endpoints. Here are the ten you will reach for most.

EndpointMethodWhat it does
/contactsGETList contacts with filters and search
/contactsPOSTCreate a new contact
/contacts/{id}PUTUpdate an existing contact
/contacts/{id}/tagsPOSTAdd tags to a contact
/contacts/{id}/notesPOSTAdd a note to a contact
/pipelinesGETList pipelines and their stages
/opportunitiesPOSTCreate a deal in a pipeline
/opportunities/{id}PUTMove a deal to another stage
/conversations/messagesPOSTSend an SMS or email
/calendars/appointmentsPOSTCreate an appointment

Real Integration 1 — Custom Website Form to GHL Contact

The most common request: a client has a custom website form (not a GHL form) and wants every submission to create a GHL contact instantly. With the GoHighLevel API you POST the form data straight to /contacts.

// Runs on your backend / serverless function — NOT in the browser
const response = await fetch('https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/contacts', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Version': '2021-07-28'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    firstName: 'Jane',
    lastName: 'Doe',
    email: 'jane@example.com',
    phone: '+15551234567',
    tags: ['website-lead'],
    source: 'Website Contact Form'
  })
});

const contact = await response.json();

Warning: never expose your API key in frontend JavaScript — anyone can read it in the browser. Always proxy the request through a backend route or serverless function so the key stays server-side.

Real Integration 2 — Property Portal Webhook to GHL

Property portals such as Rightmove, Zillow, or CoStar fire a webhook to your server every time someone enquires on a listing. You build a small receiver — a Next.js API route or an Express endpoint — to turn that enquiry into a fully tagged GHL lead with a deal attached.

  1. Receive the inbound POST from the portal.
  2. Extract the lead data (name, email, phone, property reference).
  3. Create the contact by POSTing to /contacts.
  4. Tag it via /contacts/{id}/tags with portal-lead and property-ref-{id} so reporting stays clean.
  5. Create a deal by POSTing to /opportunities named "New Enquiry" in the right pipeline stage.
  6. Return 200 so the portal knows delivery succeeded.

This gives the client a real-time lead flow with full attribution — something no native integration offers for a niche portal.

Real Integration 3 — Power BI / Google Data Studio to GHL Data

Enterprise clients often want GHL pipeline data inside their own BI dashboard. The clean approach is a scheduled export rather than a live connection.

  • Run a cron job daily at midnight.
  • Fetch all active opportunities, paginating through the results to respect the rate limit.
  • Transform the JSON into a flat CSV (one row per deal, stage and value as columns).
  • Push that file to Google Sheets or Azure Blob Storage.
  • Point Power BI or Google Data Studio at that source as its dataset.

The BI tool reads from a stable, pre-shaped source — so dashboards stay fast and you never hammer the GHL API during business hours.

Real Integration 4 — GHL to External SMS Platform

Some clients must send SMS through Twilio, MessageBird, or another approved carrier for compliance reasons rather than GHL's built-in SMS. You can route messages out while keeping GHL as the system of record.

  1. In GHL, add a Workflow with a Webhook action that fires when a message should go out.
  2. The webhook hits your custom endpoint, sending the contact and message body.
  3. Your endpoint formats the payload for the external SMS API and sends it.
  4. It then logs the delivery status back to the GHL contact as a note via /contacts/{id}/notes.

The agent sees a clean audit trail inside GHL while the actual send happens on the compliant platform.

GHL Webhooks — Receiving Events From GHL

Beyond calling the API, you can have GHL push events to you in real time. Go to Location Settings > Webhooks > Add Webhook URL and point it at your endpoint. Available events include:

  • ContactCreated, ContactUpdated, ContactDeleted
  • OpportunityCreated, OpportunityUpdated, OpportunityStageChanged
  • AppointmentCreated, AppointmentUpdated
  • FormSubmitted, SurveySubmitted
  • InboundMessage, OutboundMessage
  • InvoicePaid

The golden rule for webhook receivers: always return a 200 quickly. If you need to do heavy work, acknowledge the event first and process it asynchronously on a queue so GHL does not time out and retry.

When to Hire a GHL Developer vs Using Zapier

Zapier is excellent for the right job — but it has hard limits. Use this as a quick decision guide.

Use Zapier when…Use custom API development when…
A native integration already existsNo native integration exists for the platform
You need it working todayYou need real-time events, not polling
Volume is under 1,000 tasks per monthYou have high volume that makes per-task pricing painful
The data maps one-to-oneYou need complex transformation or branching logic
No special compliance constraintsSecurity or compliance requires data stays in your control

If you are stuck on the right side of that table, that is exactly where custom GHL API development pays for itself — and where the GHL Prime team lives.

blogPosts.title: Advanced GoHighLevel Zapier Workflows: Multi-Step Automations for Agencies
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Build advanced multi-step Zapier workflows for GoHighLevel: Stripe onboarding, DocuSign sync, Typeform scoring, automated reporting, and instant lead assignment.
blogPosts.content:
Once the basics are working, it is time to level up. These advanced multi-step Zaps handle full client onboarding, payment-triggered pipeline moves, contract-to-CRM sync, and automated weekly reporting — the kind of orchestration that makes an agency feel ten people deep. At GHL Prime we run each of these workflows in live client accounts, so the patterns below are battle-tested, not theoretical. Here is exactly how to build them.

Advanced Workflow 1 — Full Client Onboarding on Stripe Payment

The moment a client's payment clears, an entire onboarding sequence should fire without anyone lifting a finger. This six-step Zap turns a Stripe charge into a fully onboarded contact, complete with internal alerts and a tracker update.

  1. Stripe — Payment Succeeded (add a Filter by Zapier so it only continues when product = "Agency Retainer").
  2. HighLevel — Create Contact and apply the tag new-client.
  3. HighLevel — Add to Pipeline "Client Onboarding" at the first stage.
  4. Gmail / Outlook — Send Welcome Email with the onboarding document attached or linked.
  5. Slack — Post Message to #new-clients announcing the signed account.
  6. Google Sheets — Create Spreadsheet Row in your Active Clients tracker.

The result: the entire onboarding runs the second the payment clears. Your delivery team sees the Slack ping, the welcome email is already in the client's inbox, and the CRM and tracker are in sync — all before a human reads the notification.

Advanced Workflow 2 — DocuSign Contract Signed to GHL Pipeline Move

Contracts are a classic point where deals stall in the CRM. This four-step Zap closes the gap between "they signed" and "the pipeline reflects it" instantly.

  1. DocuSign — Envelope Completed triggers when all parties have signed.
  2. HighLevel — Find Contact by the signer's email address.
  3. HighLevel — Update Pipeline Stage to "Contract Signed".
  4. HighLevel — Add Tag + Send SMS: "Your contract is confirmed — we'll be in touch within 24 hours."

Using Find Contact instead of Create avoids duplicate records, since the lead almost always already exists in your CRM by the time they sign.

Advanced Workflow 3 — Typeform Multi-Page Form to GHL Contact + Scoring

Not every lead deserves the same response. This five-step Zap scores leads on the way in and routes the best ones straight to a senior rep.

  1. Typeform — New Submission from your multi-page intake form.
  2. Formatter by Zapier calculates a lead score: budget > $1k = high and timeline < 1 month = high.
  3. HighLevel — Create Contact mapping all submitted fields.
  4. Filter by Zapier — continue only if the score evaluates to High.
  5. HighLevel — Add Tag high-value-lead and assign to a senior rep via a task.

Low-scoring leads still land in the CRM at step 3 — they simply do not trigger the senior-rep escalation. That keeps your best closers focused on the prospects most likely to convert.

Advanced Workflow 4 — Weekly GHL Report to Google Sheets

Reporting is the task everyone forgets until Friday afternoon. Automate it with a scheduled Zap that runs while you sleep.

  1. Schedule by Zapier — every Monday at 8:00 am.
  2. HighLevel — Search Contacts created in the last 7 days.
  3. Google Sheets — Create Spreadsheet Row with the weekly summary numbers.
  4. Slack — Post Message to #weekly-report with the headline metrics.

This is a high-level pulse, not a forensic report. Combine it with GHL's native reporting and Google Data Studio (Looker Studio) when you need drill-down detail and visual dashboards for client reviews.

Advanced Workflow 5 — Facebook Lead Ad to GHL to Instant Call Assignment

Speed-to-lead is everything on paid traffic. This six-step Zap gets a rep dialing a fresh Facebook lead in under 60 seconds.

  1. Facebook Lead Ads — New Lead fires the instant a form is submitted.
  2. HighLevel — Create Contact with the tag facebook-lead.
  3. HighLevel — Add to Pipeline "New Lead".
  4. HighLevel — Create Task assigned to a rep, due now.
  5. Slack — Send Direct Message to the rep with the lead's details and phone number.
  6. HighLevel — Send SMS immediately to the new lead acknowledging their inquiry.

The total elapsed time from form submission to a rep being notified with a phone number is under 60 seconds — which is the difference between a connected call and a cold voicemail.

Zapier Paths — Running Different Workflows Based on GHL Data

Once you outgrow one-size-fits-all Zaps, Paths (available on Zapier's paid plans) let a single Zap branch into different action sequences based on a condition. A new GHL contact can flow down completely different routes depending on its segment:

  • Path A — enterprise: assign to a senior rep and fire a Slack alert to the leadership channel.
  • Path B — small-business: drop into an automated nurture sequence.
  • Path C — competitor: route into a long-term drip only, no sales touch.

Paths keep your automation library lean — one well-built Zap with three branches beats three brittle Zaps you have to keep in sync.

Monitoring and Maintaining Your Zaps

Advanced automation is only an asset if it keeps running. Build a maintenance habit around these four practices:

  • Check task history weekly to spot silent failures or unexpected skips.
  • Turn on error notifications so Zapier emails you the moment a Zap fails.
  • Use version history to roll back when a "small" edit breaks a working Zap.
  • Document every Zap in a shared sheet — name, trigger, actions, owner, and last tested date.

That documentation sheet is what separates a fragile stack from a maintainable one. When a team member leaves or an app changes its API, you want a single source of truth, not a scavenger hunt through 40 untitled Zaps.

SaaS Mode is the feature that turns GoHighLevel from an agency tool into a software business you can resell under your own brand. Instead of charging one-off setup fees, you package the platform, set your own monthly price, and let GoHighLevel handle provisioning and billing automatically.

This guide walks through enabling SaaS Mode end to end so every new client becomes a recurring, automated subscription instead of a manual project.

Before you start

SaaS Mode requires the GoHighLevel $497/month Agency Pro plan and a connected Stripe account. You will also need rebilling enabled if you want to mark up usage-based features like SMS, email, and AI.

  • Confirm you are on the Agency Pro ($497) plan.
  • Connect your agency Stripe account under Settings > Company Billing.
  • Decide on your plan tiers and monthly pricing before you build them.

Step-by-step setup

Once the prerequisites are in place, the configuration itself is straightforward:

  • Enable SaaS Mode from the agency dashboard and connect Stripe when prompted.
  • Create your plans with clear feature gates — control which sub-account features each tier unlocks.
  • Configure rebilling so SMS, email, phone, and AI usage are marked up and passed through to clients automatically.
  • Build a SaaS configurator funnel so prospects can sign up, pay, and self-provision a sub-account without you touching anything.
  • Set up a snapshot that loads into every new account so clients start with pipelines, automations, and calendars already built.

Common mistakes to avoid

The most common failure point is pricing below your true cost. Always account for rebilling markups and platform fees so each subscriber is profitable from day one. The second is shipping an empty snapshot — clients churn fast when they log in to a blank account, so invest in a strong default snapshot before you open the doors.

With SaaS Mode configured correctly, you stop trading hours for setup fees and start building predictable monthly recurring revenue under your own brand.

blogPosts.title: GoHighLevel SaaS Mode: The Complete Setup Guide for Agency Owners (2026)
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: A step-by-step 2026 guide to setting up GoHighLevel SaaS Mode — Stripe billing, white-label branding, pricing plans and snapshots — from agency that has built 40+.
blogPosts.content:
Turning GoHighLevel into your own white-label SaaS product is one of the highest-leverage moves an agency can make — but the setup trips up most first-timers. At GHL Prime we have configured over 40 SaaS Mode accounts, and the same handful of decisions separate a smooth launch from a billing nightmare. This guide walks you through the complete 2026 setup, end to end, so you can resell GoHighLevel under your own brand with confidence.

What Is GoHighLevel SaaS Mode?

SaaS Mode is the feature inside GoHighLevel that lets you resell the platform as your own software product. Instead of being a service provider who logs in for clients, you become a software company: clients pay you a recurring subscription and log into a CRM that carries your logo, your colours, and your domain.

SaaS Mode requires the $497/mo Pro plan. That tier unlocks the SaaS Configurator, Stripe rebilling, and the ability to provision sub-accounts automatically when someone subscribes to one of your plans.

The appeal is simple: you white-label GoHighLevel and sell it as your own CRM at a markup. Your clients never see "GoHighLevel" — they see your brand — and you keep the difference between what you pay HighLevel and what you charge them every single month.

What You Need Before You Start

Get these in place before you touch the configurator. Missing one of them is the most common reason a launch stalls.

  • An active GHL Pro plan ($497/mo) — SaaS Mode is locked behind this tier.
  • A Stripe account connected to your agency for billing and rebilling.
  • Your own domain (you will point a subdomain like app.youragency.com at GHL).
  • Your logo and brand colours in usable formats (PNG/SVG logo, hex codes).
  • A pricing decision — what you will charge and what each tier includes.

Step 1 — Enable SaaS Mode in Your Agency Dashboard

From your agency view, go to Settings → SaaS Configurator → Enable. This switches the agency from standard mode into a software business and reveals the rebilling and plan-creation tools you will use in the next steps.

[Image: SaaS Mode toggle in GHL settings]

Once enabled, the SaaS Configurator becomes your control centre for plans, branding, and client provisioning. Nothing is live to clients yet — you are simply unlocking the build.

Step 2 — Connect Stripe for Billing

SaaS Mode bills your clients through Stripe, so connect your Stripe account from the SaaS Configurator. This is what charges clients monthly and, through rebilling, lets you mark up usage-based items like SMS, email, and AI.

Pay close attention to test mode versus live mode. Stripe defaults to test mode while you build, and test-mode keys will never charge a real card. Before you onboard a paying client, confirm you have switched to live keys — shipping with test keys is one of the most common (and most expensive) launch mistakes.

Step 3 — Set Up Your Pricing Plans

Most agencies run three tiers. Here is a proven structure:

  • Starter — $97/mo: core CRM, contacts, pipelines, calendar, and basic email/SMS. Ideal for solo operators getting started.
  • Growth — $197/mo: everything in Starter plus workflow automation, funnels, and review management. This is where most clients land.
  • Pro — $297/mo: everything in Growth plus AI features (Conversation AI, Voice AI), advanced reporting, and higher rebilling allowances.

Create each plan in the SaaS Configurator and attach the right feature set. The bigger the gap in value between tiers, the easier it is to upsell clients upward over time.

Step 4 — Configure Your White-Label Branding

This is where GoHighLevel disappears and your brand takes over. In the SaaS settings, upload your logo, set your brand colours, and configure your custom domain so clients log in at app.youragency.com instead of a HighLevel URL.

To point your domain at GHL:

  1. In your DNS provider, create a CNAME record for the subdomain (e.g. app).
  2. Point that CNAME at the target GoHighLevel gives you in the white-label settings.
  3. Save the record and allow DNS to propagate (usually minutes, occasionally up to a few hours).
  4. Back in GHL, verify the domain — once it resolves, your branded login is live.

From this point on, clients experience a CRM that looks entirely like your own software.

Step 5 — Build Your Snapshot

A snapshot is a pre-built template of everything a new sub-account should start with: pipelines, workflows, calendars, and funnels. When you provision a client, the snapshot loads instantly so they get a working system on day one instead of an empty CRM.

A strong snapshot is the difference between clients who stick and clients who churn — it is the product they are actually paying for. GHL Prime builds custom snapshots tailored to your niche, so every client you onboard launches with a proven, ready-to-run system.

Step 6 — Invite Your First Client

With plans, branding, and a snapshot in place, you are ready to onboard. Create the sub-account, assign the appropriate pricing plan, load your snapshot, and send the client their branded login details. From their first session they will see your logo, your domain, and a fully configured CRM — and Stripe will handle the recurring billing automatically.

Common SaaS Mode Mistakes to Avoid

  • Onboarding with no snapshot — handing clients an empty CRM guarantees confusion and churn.
  • Running test-mode Stripe in production — you will never collect a payment until you switch to live keys.
  • Skipping the custom domain — a HighLevel URL breaks the white-label illusion instantly.
  • Pricing too low — undercharging leaves no margin to support clients and grow.
  • No onboarding automation — without a welcome sequence, new clients stall before they see value.

How Long Does SaaS Mode Setup Take?

An experienced operator who has done it before can stand up a clean SaaS Mode account in 3–5 days. A first-timer learning the configurator, DNS, Stripe rebilling, and snapshot building usually needs 2–4 weeks — most of that lost to trial and error. GHL Prime delivers complete, tested SaaS Mode accounts in 1–2 weeks, snapshot included.

SaaS Mode is the cleanest path from "agency that does the work" to "software company with recurring revenue." Get the foundation right — Pro plan, live Stripe, custom domain, and a real snapshot — and you have a product you can sell at scale. Rush it, and you spend your first month firefighting billing and onboarding instead of closing clients.

Why Property Developers Use GoHighLevel

blogPosts.title: How to Build a GoHighLevel AI Voice Receptionist for Your Agency Clients
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Build a GoHighLevel AI voice receptionist that answers calls 24/7, qualifies leads and books appointments automatically — built and tested by GHL Prime.
blogPosts.content:
Missed calls are the number one revenue leak for service businesses — every unanswered ring is a customer dialing your competitor. A GoHighLevel AI voice receptionist closes that gap: it answers calls 24/7, qualifies the caller, and books appointments straight into your calendar without a human picking up. GHL Prime has deployed more than 20 voice AI agents across home services, real estate, and healthcare, and this guide shows you exactly how to build one.

What Is a GoHighLevel Voice AI Agent?

Voice AI is now native to GoHighLevel on the Pro plan — no third-party glue required. The agent answers an inbound call, talks to the caller in natural language, and takes action based on a script you define.

It can: answer calls around the clock, qualify the caller, capture their details, book directly into your GHL calendar, and send a follow-up SMS. It cannot: handle complex objections or replace a skilled closer. Treat it as a brilliant first responder, not a salesperson.

When to Use a GHL Voice AI Receptionist

  • After-hours coverage — capture calls that would otherwise go to voicemail and die.
  • High call volume — HVAC, plumbing, roofing, and real estate teams that can't answer every ring.
  • Qualifying inbound — filter and qualify callers before a human ever gets involved.
  • Appointment booking — let the agent fill your calendar automatically.

What You Need Before Building

  • An active GHL Pro plan (Voice AI is gated behind it).
  • A phone number — either a Twilio number connected to GHL or a GHL built-in number.
  • A configured GHL calendar for the agent to book into.
  • A clear script — the single biggest factor in whether the agent performs.

Step 1 — Enable Voice AI in GHL Settings

Go to Settings → Voice AI → Enable. This activates the agent builder and the built-in test call feature, which you will use later to dial the agent yourself and hear exactly what a caller hears.

Step 2 — Write Your Agent's Call Script

This is the most important step. The script controls the greeting, the qualification flow, and what happens when the agent hits its limits. Keep it tight: a warm greeting, a maximum of three qualification questions (service needed, location, timeline), a clear offer to book, and a fallback to a human.

Sample script — home services business

"Thanks for calling [Company Name], this is the virtual assistant. I can help you get booked in right away. First, what service do you need today — heating, cooling, or something else?"

"Great. And what's the postcode or area you're located in?"

"Perfect. Is this something you need urgently, or are you planning ahead?"

"I can get you booked with one of our technicians. Let me find the next available slot... I'll also text you a confirmation. If you'd rather speak to someone directly, just say 'speak to a person' and I'll transfer you."

Step 3 — Connect to Your GHL Calendar

Link the agent to the calendar it should book into. Define the available slots, set a buffer between appointments so technicians have travel time, and turn on an automatic confirmation SMS so the caller leaves the call with a booking in hand.

Step 4 — Set Up Call Routing

The agent should know when to hand off. Configure a transfer to a human when the caller asks for a person, when a booking fails twice, or when the request is clearly out of scope. Smart routing keeps the AI on the work it does well and protects the caller experience.

Step 5 — Test Your Agent

Before going live, call the number and check five things:

  1. Greeting clarity — does it sound natural and on-brand?
  2. Question flow — does it ask the right questions in order without rambling?
  3. Booking success — can it actually place an appointment on the calendar?
  4. SMS confirmation — does the caller receive the confirmation text?
  5. Contact created — does a new contact appear in GHL with the captured details?

Real Results — What to Expect

A well-built agent handles 60–80% of after-hours calls without a human and typically books 3–5 new appointments per week that would otherwise have been lost. One HVAC client of ours recovered roughly $12,000 in its first month simply by capturing the calls that used to hit voicemail.

Voice AI Limitations to Know

Be honest about the boundaries. Voice AI is excellent at simple qualification and booking, but it struggles with complex, emotional, or highly nuanced conversations. The right framing is "first responder, not closer" — let the AI capture and qualify every call, then route the high-intent or complicated ones to a human who can close.

blogPosts.title: Twilio SMS Not Delivering in LeadConnector: Common Problems, Error Codes and Fixes
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Your message says "Delivered" but the contact never got it? A complete guide to Twilio error codes, carrier filtering, A2P issues, and exact fixes.
blogPosts.content:
You sent the message. LeadConnector says "Delivered" in green. But the contact swears they never received it. Or you're staring at an error code like 30007 that means absolutely nothing to you. Or — worst of all — your SMS worked perfectly last month and now it's silently broken with no warning. SMS delivery issues with Twilio inside LeadConnector are frustratingly common, but the good news is they're almost always fixable once you know what's happening behind the scenes. This guide covers every common problem: the actual error codes, what they mean, what causes them, and the exact steps to fix each one. Bookmark it — you'll come back to it.

Understanding the SMS Delivery Chain

Before you can diagnose a delivery failure, you need to understand that an SMS passes through four distinct stages. A failure can happen at any point in this chain — and the error code tells you exactly where.

  1. LeadConnector queues the message and hands it to the Twilio API. Your workflow, conversation, or bulk send pushes the message into Twilio's outbound queue.
  2. Twilio passes the message to the carrier network. Twilio routes it toward the appropriate aggregator and carrier gateway.
  3. The carrier routes it to the recipient's carrier. If you're texting a Verizon number, the message has to traverse to Verizon's network.
  4. The recipient's carrier delivers it to the handset. This is the final hop — and the one with the least visibility.

Here is the single most important thing to understand: when LeadConnector shows "Delivered", that only means Twilio accepted the message — it does not mean the recipient received it. Inside Twilio, the "delivered" status means the message reached the carrier, not the handset. True handset delivery confirmation requires a DLR (Delivery Receipt) from the carrier — and not every carrier provides accurate DLRs. This gap between "accepted" and "received" is where most mysterious failures live.

How to Check Twilio Message Logs

You can't fix what you can't see. The first move on any delivery problem is to pull the logs.

If you have direct Twilio account access:

  1. Go to console.twilio.com.
  2. Navigate to Monitor > Logs > Messaging.
  3. Filter by date range, the sending number, or the recipient number.
  4. Click any individual message to open its detail view. You'll see the Error Code, the carrier response, the message status, and the full delivery timeline.

If you only have LeadConnector access (no Twilio login):

  • Go to Settings > Phone Numbers > Message History if it's available in your account.
  • Otherwise, open the individual contact's conversation log — a failed message will show a failed status, often with the underlying error code.
  • Error codes appear either in the dedicated Error Code column or inside the message detail when you hover or click on the failed message.

Once you have the error code, match it against the reference below.

Complete Twilio Error Code Reference for LeadConnector Users

Each error below tells you what it means, the common cause, and the exact fix. Find your code and follow the steps.

Error 30001 — Queue Overflow

What it means: Twilio's outbound queue for your number filled up before the message could be sent. Common cause: You're sending faster than your number's throughput allows — typically during a bulk blast. Fix: Reduce your send rate, add delays between messages in your workflow, upgrade your messaging tier or use a Messaging Service with more numbers, and spread bulk sends out over a longer window instead of firing them all at once.

Error 30002 — Account Suspended

What it means: Your Twilio sub-account has been suspended — zero SMS will send until it's resolved. Common cause: A payment failure, a Terms of Service violation, spam complaints, or sending from unregistered numbers. Fix: Log into the Twilio console immediately and check the account status banner. Resolve any outstanding billing issue first; if the suspension is for a policy reason, contact Twilio support directly to appeal. This is serious — treat it as your top priority.

Error 30003 — Unreachable Destination Handset

What it means: The destination handset couldn't be reached. Common cause: The phone is powered off, out of coverage, or the number is actually a landline. Fix: Verify the number is correct, validate whether it's a landline, and check the mobile type. For a single contact, simply retry later; if it's widespread across a list, your list quality is the problem.

Error 30004 — Message Blocked

What it means: The carrier issued a hard block on the message. Common cause: The recipient blocked your number, the carrier flagged it as spam, or the content triggered a block. Fix: Confirm you're not sending to non-opted-in contacts, review your copy for spam trigger words like FREE, WINNER, CASH, GUARANTEED, and CLICK HERE, and check your number's reputation. If the number is permanently blocked, retire it and provision a new one.

Error 30005 — Unknown Destination Handset

What it means: The number doesn't exist on the carrier network. Common cause: The number is disconnected, was ported and is no longer valid, or there's a typo. Fix: Clean your contact list, mark the number invalid so you stop retrying it, and validate your full list quarterly to remove dead numbers.

Error 30006 — Landline or Unreachable Carrier

What it means: The destination is a landline or sits on a carrier with no SMS support. Common cause: Landline numbers in your database that were never validated. Fix: Add number-type validation at the point of capture and filter landlines out of your SMS audiences entirely.

Error 30007 — Carrier Violation (Message Filtered)

What it means: This is the most common delivery failure. The carrier filtered your message before it ever reached the handset — it was silently dropped. Common causes: Your A2P campaign isn't registered or is inactive, the sending number isn't associated with the campaign, the content triggers spam filters, you used a public URL shortener (bit.ly, tinyurl), you used spam keywords, or your send timing looks suspicious.

Fix — work through these in order:

  1. Verify your A2P registration is complete and the campaign shows active.
  2. Fix the content: remove all URL shorteners, strip spam trigger words, and clearly identify your business by name.
  3. Review your send patterns — sudden volume spikes look like spam.
  4. Test delivery to a different carrier to isolate whether it's carrier-specific.
  5. If the number is burned, retire it, provision a replacement, and warm it gradually.
Error 30008 — Unknown Error

What it means: The carrier rejected the message but gave no specific reason. Common cause: A transient carrier issue or an unspecified filter. Fix: Retry the message after 30 to 60 minutes. If it persists, treat it exactly like a 30007 (assume content or A2P filtering). If you see a sudden, widespread spike of 30008s, check status.twilio.com for a platform-wide incident.

Error 30009 — Missing Inbound Segment

What it means: An inbound MMS message is missing a segment. Common cause: A multi-part MMS didn't fully arrive. Fix: Check your MMS settings and confirm the receiving number is MMS-enabled.

Error 30034 — Message Blocked Due to A2P Requirements

What it means: This is the most critical code to understand. It's a definitive A2P compliance block — fundamentally different from a 30007 content filter. The carrier is telling you the sending number is not properly registered for application-to-person messaging. Common cause: An unregistered brand, an unregistered or unapproved campaign, or a number that isn't associated with any campaign.

Fix:

  1. Complete your brand registration with The Campaign Registry (TCR).
  2. Submit your campaign and wait for approval.
  3. Associate every sending number with the approved campaign.
  4. Allow 24 to 48 hours for the registration to propagate across carriers.
  5. Stop sending from any unregistered number immediately — repeated 30034 errors permanently damage your number's reputation.
Error 21211 — Invalid 'To' Phone Number

What it means: The destination number is in an invalid format. Common cause: The number is missing the country code or has stray characters. Fix: Always store and send numbers in E.164 format — that means +1XXXXXXXXXX for the US (a plus sign, country code, then the 10-digit number with no spaces, dashes, or parentheses).

Error 21614 — 'To' Number Cannot Receive SMS

What it means: The destination number is incapable of receiving SMS. Common cause: It's a landline or a VOIP number with no SMS support. Fix: Validate the number type and remove it from SMS audiences — handle it the same way you would a 30006.

The Silent Killer — "Delivered" But Not Received

This is the scenario that makes people doubt their sanity. The status reads "Delivered" but the contact never got the text. Here's what's actually happening: "delivered" means Twilio accepted the message and it reached the carrier — but the handset state is unknown unless a true DLR comes back. Carrier-level filtering can happen silently after Twilio has already marked the message delivered, so it shows green on your end while the carrier quietly drops it.

How to diagnose it:

  • Send a test to a phone you control on the same carrier as the contact who isn't receiving messages. If you get it, the problem is contact-specific; if you don't, it's a carrier or content issue.
  • Check your content for filter triggers — shorteners, spam words, all-caps.
  • Confirm your A2P registration is fully active, not just "submitted."
  • Ask the contact to check their blocked or spam SMS folder — on Android, filtered messages often land in a separate spam folder.
  • Send the same content from a different, fully registered number to see if the original number is the culprit.

Content Issues That Cause Carrier Filtering

Carriers run every message through automated content filters. These are the patterns that get you dropped.

Blocked URL patterns: Public link shorteners like bit.ly, tinyurl.com, and t.co are heavily filtered because spammers abuse them. Use full URLs, or set up a custom shortener on your own domain.

Trigger words and formatting:

  • FREE in all caps
  • WINNER, CONGRATULATIONS, YOU HAVE BEEN SELECTED
  • CASH, EARN MONEY, MAKE MONEY
  • CLICK HERE, TAP HERE
  • GUARANTEED, RISK FREE
  • URGENT, ACT NOW, LIMITED TIME
  • Excessive punctuation like !!! or ???
  • Writing entire messages in ALL CAPS

What carriers actually want to see:

  • Your business name clearly identified in the message
  • A clear opt-out — Reply STOP to unsubscribe
  • A consistent sender number
  • Relevant content that matches what the contact signed up for
  • Normal mixed-case writing, not shouting in all caps

Number Reputation and Warming

Every Twilio number carries a carrier reputation score that builds over time based on your sending behavior. Burn it and your delivery collapses.

Signs of a damaged number:

  • Consistently high 30007 errors
  • Delivery rate below 70%
  • A sudden drop after the number was previously working fine
  • Non-delivery across multiple carriers, not just one

How to warm a brand-new number — ramp volume gradually so carriers learn to trust it:

PeriodDaily Send Volume
Day 1–350–100 messages/day
Day 4–7200–300 messages/day
Week 2500–1,000 messages/day
Week 3+Scale up from there

Blasting 5,000 messages from a number on day one is the fastest way to get it flagged and blocked. Patience here pays off in long-term deliverability.

Twilio + LeadConnector Specific Issues

Some problems are specific to running Twilio inside LeadConnector. Here are the common ones and their fixes.

  • The number shows "Active" but SMS still fails. The campaign association may have expired, or the monthly A2P fee failed to charge. Check your A2P status, renew the fee, and re-associate the number with the campaign.
  • It works for some contacts but not others. This is carrier-specific filtering — for example, it fails on Verizon but works on T-Mobile. Pull your logs, identify the failing carrier, and contact Twilio with the logs and the carrier name.
  • Inbound works but outbound fails. Outbound A2P messaging requires full registration; inbound does not. Complete your A2P registration to fix outbound.
  • MMS fails but SMS works. Either the number isn't MMS-enabled or the media file exceeds 5MB. Verify the number is MMS-capable, compress your media, and host it on a public URL.

When to Escalate to Twilio Support Directly

Most issues you can fix yourself. Escalate to Twilio when:

  • Your account has been suspended.
  • You keep getting 30034 even after completing A2P registration and waiting for propagation.
  • You see 30007 on all messages across multiple numbers.
  • You hit a sudden total failure with no configuration changes on your end.

To get a fast resolution, include all of this in your ticket:

  • Your Twilio account SID (or the LeadConnector sub-account ID)
  • The exact error code
  • The sending number SID
  • Example message SIDs that failed
  • Screenshots of your A2P registration status
  • A timeline of when it started and what changed

Twilio's standard response time is 24 to 48 hours, so include everything up front to avoid a back-and-forth.

Complete SMS Troubleshooting Checklist

Run through this top to bottom whenever delivery breaks.

A2P Registration

  • [ ] Is your brand approved?
  • [ ] Is your campaign active?
  • [ ] Is every sending number associated with the campaign?
  • [ ] Is the monthly A2P fee current?

Message Content

  • [ ] No public URL shorteners?
  • [ ] No all-caps trigger words?
  • [ ] Business name included?
  • [ ] STOP / opt-out language present?
  • [ ] Under 160 characters?

Number Health

  • [ ] Is the number mobile-capable?
  • [ ] Was it warmed gradually?
  • [ ] No history of spam complaints?

Recipient

  • [ ] Number in E.164 format (+1XXXXXXXXXX)?
  • [ ] Has the recipient not previously replied STOP?
  • [ ] Is it not a landline or VOIP number?

Account

  • [ ] Is the Twilio account in good standing?
  • [ ] No LeadConnector payment failures?
  • [ ] Are you within your throughput limits?

blogPosts.title: A2P 10DLC Registration in LeadConnector: Complete Guide, Common Errors and How to Fix Them
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: The definitive A2P 10DLC guide for LeadConnector: brand and campaign registration, every common error and fix, and how to get approved fast in 2026.
blogPosts.content:
SMS suddenly blocked. Campaigns stuck on "pending" for weeks. A2P submissions rejected for reasons nobody explains clearly. If that sounds familiar, you are not alone — A2P 10DLC compliance is one of the most frustrating technical hurdles any business sending text messages through software faces today. Here is the thing most people never realize: LeadConnector does not actually deliver your SMS. It uses Twilio as its underlying carrier, and Twilio relies on The Campaign Registry (TCR) to verify every 10DLC message campaign in the United States. Understanding this three-layer system — LeadConnector > Twilio > TCR — is the single key to getting approved. This guide explains exactly what A2P 10DLC is, the precise registration steps inside LeadConnector, every common error and how to fix it, and what to do when you are completely stuck.

What Is A2P 10DLC and Why Does It Exist?

A2P stands for Application-to-Person — messages sent by software to individual people. This is the opposite of P2P (Person-to-Person), where one human texts another from their phone. When you send appointment reminders, lead follow-ups, or promotional offers from LeadConnector, you are sending A2P traffic, even though the messages come from a normal-looking phone number.

10DLC stands for 10-Digit Long Code — a standard US phone number like 555-123-4567. This is distinct from short codes (5–6 digit numbers like 12345) and toll-free numbers (800, 833, 844, and similar). A 10DLC number gives you a local presence while still being approved for high-volume application traffic — once it is registered.

So why does any of this exist? Before 2021, businesses blasted marketing texts from ordinary long codes with no oversight, and spam exploded. The major US carriers — AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile — responded by aggressively blocking entire ranges of unregistered traffic. The carriers and the industry introduced the 10DLC framework in 2021 as the fix: businesses register their identity, declare what kind of content they send, document how recipients opted in, and in exchange the carriers agree to let those messages through reliably.

Enforcement runs through a chain. The Campaign Registry (TCR) is the central hub that stores every brand and campaign. The carriers read TCR data and decide to accept or reject your traffic. Twilio is a registered Campaign Service Provider (CSP) that submits your registration to TCR on your behalf. The full chain looks like this: LeadConnector > Twilio > TCR > Carriers.

What happens if you skip registration? Your messages get silently filtered at the carrier level. This is the silent killer of SMS marketing: LeadConnector and Twilio may show the message as "delivered" or "sent," but the recipient's carrier quietly drops it and the person never sees a thing. You think your campaign is working. It is not.

The Three Components of A2P 10DLC Registration

A2P 10DLC registration is not one step — it is three distinct pieces that must all be completed and linked together.

1. Brand Registration — Who You Are

This establishes your business identity with TCR. Required fields:

  • Legal business name — must match your EIN documentation exactly
  • Business type — Private, Public, Non-profit, or Government
  • EIN (Employer Identification Number) — US businesses only
  • Business address
  • Website URL
  • Industry vertical
  • Contact name, email, and phone

Cost: $4 one-time registration fee. Processing: typically 24–72 hours, occasionally up to 7 days.

2. Campaign Registration — What You Send

This declares the type of messages you will send. Required fields:

  • Use case — Marketing, Account Notifications, Customer Care, 2FA, or Mixed
  • Campaign description — 2–3 sentences, reviewed by a human at TCR
  • 2–3 sample messages representative of what you actually send
  • Opt-in method description — how people consent
  • Opt-in keywords — START, YES, SUBSCRIBE
  • Opt-out keywords — STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT
  • Help keywords — HELP, INFO

Cost: $10–$15 per month per campaign. Processing: 3–7 business days, occasionally up to 21 days for higher-scrutiny use cases.

3. Number Association — Connecting It All

Finally, you must associate your approved 10DLC phone numbers with your approved campaign. This is the step most people forget. A number that is not associated with an active campaign gets filtered exactly as if you never registered at all.

Step-by-Step A2P Registration in LeadConnector

Step 1 — Navigate to A2P Registration

Go to Settings > Phone Numbers > SMS Registration > A2P Registration. The exact location varies between LeadConnector versions and white-label builds — look for any menu item labeled "A2P," "10DLC," or "SMS Compliance."

Step 2 — Brand Registration

Click Register Brand and complete the form carefully:

  • Legal name — enter it exactly as it appears on your IRS EIN confirmation letter, including the suffix (LLC, Inc., Corp.)
  • EIN — 9 digits, no dashes
  • Business type — select the correct classification
  • Address — your registered business address, not a virtual office or mailbox service
  • Website — a live site that clearly references the business
  • Industry — your vertical

Submit and wait. Status moves from Pending to either Approved or Failed.

Step 3 — Create Your Campaign

Choosing the right use case matters more than people think:

  • Mixed — covers multiple message types; the most flexible option, which is why most agencies choose it
  • Marketing — promotional content only; highest scrutiny and slowest review
  • Account Notifications — reminders and updates; lower scrutiny, faster approval
  • Customer Care — support conversations
  • 2FA — authentication codes only

Now write your campaign description. This is reviewed by a human, and vagueness gets you rejected.

BAD example: "We send marketing messages to our customers."

GOOD example: "We send appointment reminders, lead follow-up messages, and promotional offers to contacts who have opted in via our website contact form and landing pages. All contacts have provided explicit written consent prior to receiving messages."

Your sample messages must be realistic, include opt-out language, and match your use case. Three concrete examples:

  1. "Hi {first name}, this is Sarah from Apex Roofing following up on your free estimate request. Are you still looking to get that quote scheduled? Reply STOP to opt out."
  2. "Reminder: your appointment with Apex Roofing is tomorrow at 2:00 PM. Reply C to confirm or R to reschedule. Reply STOP to unsubscribe."
  3. "Your custom roofing quote is ready, {first name}. View it here: https://apexroofing.com/quote/12345 — Reply STOP to opt out."

Your opt-in description is the field that gets the most campaigns rejected.

BAD: "Customers opt in online."

GOOD: "Contacts provide their phone number and check a consent checkbox on our website contact form at https://apexroofing.com/contact. The checkbox states: 'I agree to receive SMS messages from Apex Roofing. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.'"

Step 4 — Associate Phone Numbers

Go to Phone Numbers, select a number, choose Associate with Campaign, select your approved campaign, and click Save. Repeat for every number you intend to send from.

Step 5 — Verify Everything Is Active

You need all three states green before a single message will deliver reliably:

  • [ ] Brand status: Approved
  • [ ] Campaign status: Active
  • [ ] Number: Associated with the active campaign

Common A2P Registration Errors in LeadConnector and How to Fix Them

Brand Registration Failed — EIN Mismatch

Cause: The legal business name and EIN you submitted do not match IRS records. TCR cross-references this against government data, and even a tiny discrepancy fails the brand. Fix: Pull out your IRS EIN confirmation letter (CP 575 or 147C) and copy the name character-for-character. The most common mistakes are forgetting the entity suffix (LLC, Inc., Corp.), submitting a DBA or "doing business as" name instead of the registered legal name, or transposing digits in the EIN. Enter the EIN as 9 digits with no dashes.

Brand Registration Failed — Website Does Not Match Business

Cause: The website you submitted does not clearly represent the business — it is under construction, has no contact information, or does not mention the services you say you provide. Fix: Make sure the site displays the business name, has a contact page listing an address that matches your brand registration, includes a privacy policy that mentions SMS, and contains content matching the services in your campaign. Use the exact same URL format (https and www) consistently across the form.

Campaign Rejected — Insufficient Opt-In Description

Cause: Your opt-in description was too vague for the TCR reviewer to confirm that recipients gave real consent. Fix: Rewrite it to be extremely specific. Name the URL of the opt-in form, quote the exact consent checkbox wording, and state the channel — web form, point-of-sale, verbal, or paper. If consent is collected verbally (for example over the phone), specify the script your staff reads and confirm where the consent is logged.

Campaign Rejected — Sample Messages Do Not Match Use Case

Cause: You selected one use case but your sample messages clearly describe a different kind of traffic — for example a "Customer Care" campaign with samples full of promotional offers. Fix: Align the use case with your samples. If you send a mix of message types, pick the Mixed use case. Every sample message must include your business name, a clear purpose, and a STOP opt-out instruction.

Campaign Stuck in Pending More Than 10 Days

Cause: Your campaign landed in a TCR manual review queue, which can back up. Fix: First, check with LeadConnector support to confirm there is no outstanding compliance flag on your account. Verify the brand has no issues blocking the campaign. Then contact Twilio with your TCR brand ID and campaign ID to request a status check. In some cases, withdrawing the campaign and resubmitting it cleanly resets your place in the queue and triggers a faster review.

Messages Still Filtered After Approval

Cause: Either your phone number is not associated with the approved campaign, or carrier propagation has not finished. Fix: Confirm the number is associated with the active campaign, then wait up to 24 hours for the carriers to propagate the registration. Test by sending to numbers on AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile separately, since filtering can be carrier-specific. Check your Twilio message logs for the real delivery status rather than trusting the platform's "delivered" label.

Brand Approved but Campaign Won't Submit

Cause: Campaign registration carries a recurring $10–$15/month fee, and the charge failed. Fix: Check the payment method on file in your LeadConnector or Twilio billing settings, make sure it is valid and has funds, then retry the campaign submission.

Sole Proprietor Brand Registration

Cause: You do not have an EIN, so you registered as a sole proprietor. What it means: Sole proprietor brands register through a different path and carry much lower limits — roughly 1,000 messages per day versus 6,000+ for a registered business with an EIN. Fix: If you are a real business sending meaningful volume, obtain an EIN (free and fast from the IRS) and register as a standard brand instead.

A2P Compliance Requirements — What You Must Have

Approval depends on demonstrating proper consent. Your opt-in consent language must include every one of these elements:

  • The business name sending the SMS
  • A statement that message and data rates may apply
  • The message frequency (for example, "message frequency varies")
  • How to opt out — reply STOP
  • How to get help — reply HELP

Here is a fully compliant checkbox text you can adapt:

"By checking this box, you agree to receive SMS messages from [Business Name] regarding [purpose]. Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies. Reply STOP to unsubscribe or HELP for help. View our Privacy Policy at [link]."

Your website privacy policy must also address SMS specifically. It needs to state that you collect phone numbers, explain how they are used, confirm how recipients can opt out — and include the line nearly everyone forgets: that mobile opt-in data will not be shared with third parties for their own marketing purposes. Reviewers actively look for that sentence, and its absence is a frequent cause of rejection.

For the overwhelming majority of LeadConnector users, 10DLC is the right choice: it gives you a local number, reasonable cost, and solid deliverability once registered.

Daily Message Limits on 10DLC

Throughput on 10DLC is not unlimited, and it scales with your sending reputation:

  • New registered brand: roughly 2,000–6,000 messages per day per number
  • Established brand with good history: up to 75,000 messages per day
  • Sole proprietor: about 1,000 messages per day

If you need to send more than your number allows, you have two options: add more registered numbers and distribute the volume across them, or move to a short code for true high-volume national sending.

Maintaining Compliance After Registration

Approval is not the finish line. To stay compliant and keep your messages flowing:

  • Honor STOP immediately. LeadConnector automates opt-out handling, but verify it actually works by texting STOP to your own number and confirming you are removed.
  • Keep opt-in records — who consented, when, and how — for at least 4 years.
  • Update your campaign if your use case changes. Sending content that does not match your registered campaign risks new filtering.
  • Follow TCPA rules: no purchased lists, no sends between 9pm and 8am in the recipient's local time, and no marketing to numbers on the National Do Not Call Registry.
  • Monitor delivery rates. If they drop suddenly, contact Twilio — it usually signals a carrier-level filtering change.

When to Contact Twilio Directly vs LeadConnector Support

Knowing who to call saves days of back-and-forth.

Contact LeadConnector first for:

  • Messages being filtered despite an approved campaign

blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: A2P 10DLC isn't state-by-state, but state mini-TCPA laws are. Here's how GoHighLevel A2P 10DLC state compliance actually layers together for agencies texting through LeadConnector.
blogPosts.content:
If you send texts through GoHighLevel, you’ve almost certainly bumped into A2P 10DLC registration — and you may have seen scary talk about ‘state-specific’ texting rules. The two things get tangled together constantly, so let’s untangle them. The short version: A2P 10DLC is a single national carrier registration, while a handful of individual states have their own texting laws that stack on top of federal rules.

This guide explains how GoHighLevel A2P 10DLC state compliance really works, what Florida, Oklahoma, Washington and Texas actually require, and how to configure GHL so you stay on the right side of all of it. This is informational only — not legal advice. For your specific situation, talk to a qualified attorney.

What A2P 10DLC Actually Is (and Isn’t)

A2P 10DLC stands for Application-to-Person messaging over 10-Digit Long Codes — ordinary local phone numbers used to send automated or bulk business texts. To send this traffic to US recipients, carriers require registration through The Campaign Registry (TCR).

  • It’s national, not per-state. There is one TCR registration covering all US carriers. There is no ‘A2P 10DLC for Florida’ or ‘A2P 10DLC for Texas’ — the same registration applies nationwide.
  • It has two parts. First you register a Brand (your legal business: name, EIN, address, website). Then you register one or more Campaigns (your use case, sample messages, opt-in details, and volume).
  • The data has to match. Your business name, EIN and address must exactly match your IRS records, or the brand gets rejected. In 2026, TCR also tightened things: EINs generally need to be at least 15 days old, opt-in URLs must be live and verifiable, and platforms registering on behalf of clients need a reseller ID.
  • In GHL it’s LeadConnector. GoHighLevel’s built-in phone system is LeadConnector, so your A2P registration flows through the LeadConnector A2P registration process inside your sub-account.

So when someone says A2P 10DLC is ‘state-specific,’ they’re mixing it up with something real but separate: state texting laws.

The Federal Layer: TCPA

Above the carrier layer sits the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), the federal law governing marketing calls and texts. A2P registration gets your messages delivered; TCPA governs whether you’re allowed to send them. Core rules:

  • Consent before marketing. Promotional texts generally require prior express written consent — a documented, affirmative agreement to receive marketing texts from your specific business.
  • Quiet hours. Telephone solicitations are restricted to between 8am and 9pm in the recipient’s local time. Sending outside that window is a common, avoidable mistake.
  • Easy opt-out. Recipients must be able to opt out, and as of 2025 the FCC expects businesses to honor opt-out requests sent by any reasonable method — not just the keyword ‘STOP.’

The State Layer: Mini-TCPAs

Several states have passed their own texting and telemarketing laws — often called ‘mini-TCPAs’ — that go further than the federal baseline and frequently carry a private right of action, meaning consumers (and their lawyers) can sue you directly. These are where ‘state texting laws SMS’ concerns actually come from.

Florida (FTSA) — a2p 10dlc florida and the Florida mini-TCPA

The Florida Telephone Solicitation Act (FTSA) is the one most agencies worry about, and for good reason. Florida’s ‘mini-TCPA’ texting rules add real teeth:

  • Prior express written consent is required before sending sales texts to Florida consumers — though consent can be satisfied by an affirmative act like checking a box or replying to opt in.
  • A private right of action allows $500 per violation (or actual damages), tripled for willful violations. This drove a wave of class-action litigation.
  • A STOP safe harbor from 2023 amendments: if a recipient replies ‘STOP,’ you have 15 days to cease sending. Honoring opt-outs promptly is your protection.
  • Stricter timing sensibilities — Florida has historically applied narrower calling windows, so the safest approach is conservative sending hours in recipient local time.

Oklahoma (OTSA)

Oklahoma’s Telephone Solicitation Act closely mirrors Florida’s. It requires prior express written consent for sales calls and texts made with an automated system, and it provides a private right of action at $500 per violation, tripled for willful or knowing violations. If you market into Oklahoma, treat it like Florida.

Washington (CEMA)

Washington’s Commercial Electronic Mail Act (CEMA) prohibits sending commercial text messages without the recipient’s prior permission, and Washington consumers have used it (alongside the state Consumer Protection Act) to pursue claims. Again: documented consent first.

Texas

Texas is frequently misunderstood. It does not have a Florida-style mini-TCPA with the same private-right-of-action exposure. For a2p 10dlc texas purposes, the real obligation is making sure your A2P 10DLC registration is complete and accurate and that you follow federal TCPA rules. Don’t assume there’s a separate ‘Texas registration’ — there isn’t.

How to Set Up GoHighLevel for Compliance

Here’s how we configure GHL/LeadConnector accounts so they satisfy the whole stack — carrier, federal and state — rather than just one layer.

  • Complete A2P 10DLC registration properly. Submit accurate brand details that match your EIN exactly, register a campaign that truthfully describes your use case, and use real, live opt-in URLs. Cutting corners here causes rejections and delivery failures, not just compliance gaps.
  • Capture and store consent. Build opt-in into your GHL forms and funnels with clear consent language, and store the timestamp, source and IP. If you’re ever challenged, your proof of consent is your defense.
  • Honor opt-outs automatically. LeadConnector processes STOP, but go further: suppress opted-out contacts across workflows and accept other reasonable opt-out phrasing. Never let an automation re-text someone who left.
  • Set sending windows to local time. Use GHL’s scheduling so workflows only fire within safe hours in the recipient’s time zone — not yours. This single setting prevents a large share of quiet-hours risk.
  • Separate marketing from transactional. Keep promotional campaigns distinct from appointment reminders and order updates. Different consent expectations apply, and mixing them muddies your compliance posture.

FAQ

Does A2P 10DLC have separate registrations per state?

No. A2P 10DLC is a single national registration through The Campaign Registry. State texting laws are separate obligations that apply on top of it based on where your recipients are.

Do I need to register again for Florida or Texas?

No additional A2P registration exists for any state. You complete one registration and then follow federal TCPA plus any applicable state mini-TCPA rules for the states you text into.

Is honoring STOP enough?

It’s essential but not sufficient. You also need valid prior consent, correct sending hours, and a way to honor opt-outs sent in other reasonable ways.

Get Your GHL Texting Set Up Right

A2P 10DLC, TCPA and state mini-TCPAs are layers, not alternatives — and the cleanest way to handle all of them is a properly configured account from day one.
