blogPosts.excerpt: GoHighLevel covers 80% out of the box. The other 20% needs custom development. Here is what vibe coding builds that GHL can't do natively.
blogPosts.content:
GoHighLevel handles roughly 80% of what most agencies need straight out of the box: CRM, pipelines, automations, calendars, funnels, and email. The remaining 20% — custom dashboards, branded client portals, bespoke AI tools, and integrations with platforms that have no native connector — is where teams hit a wall. That gap is exactly what custom GoHighLevel development closes. At GHL Prime we call our approach vibe coding: AI-assisted development that ships production-ready custom features on top of GHL fast. Here is what it builds, when you actually need it, and what it costs in time and money.

What Is Vibe Coding in the Context of GoHighLevel?

Vibe coding is software development accelerated by modern AI tooling — Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot — used to design, write, and ship custom features dramatically faster than traditional hand-coding. It is not about replacing developers. It is about accelerating them. An experienced engineer still owns the architecture, the security model, and the GHL API integration, but the AI handles the repetitive scaffolding, boilerplate, and first-draft logic.

The practical effect is speed. A custom GHL build that would have taken a team 3-4 weeks of conventional development now ships in 5-7 days. That compression is what makes bespoke features economical for agencies that previously assumed custom work was out of reach. When the cost of building drops, the set of problems worth solving with code expands — and that is the real story of vibe coding GHL.

When Do You Actually Need Custom GHL Development?

You do not need custom development for everything — most needs are covered natively or by Zapier and Make. You need custom GHL development when you hit the genuine limits of the platform. The clearest signs:

  • You need a single dashboard combining GHL data with another platform (Google Ads, Facebook Ads, Stripe) that GHL cannot natively merge.
  • You want a branded client portal that goes far beyond a read-only GHL snapshot.
  • You need an integration that does not exist in Zapier or Make, or one too complex for no-code tooling.
  • You want AI features beyond Conversation AI — custom prompts, conversation-history context, multi-step generation.
  • You need custom reporting that native GHL reports simply cannot produce.
  • You have a business process that does not fit GHL pipelines and forcing it in creates more work than it saves.

If two or more of these describe your situation, custom development is usually the right call.

Custom Build 1 — White-Label Client Reporting Dashboard

This is a fully branded web application that pulls live GHL data through the GoHighLevel API and presents it under your logo, your colors, and your own domain. Your clients log in and see one clean view of their entire marketing performance.

What GHL can't do: combine GHL pipeline data with Google Ads spend, Facebook Ads results, and Stripe revenue inside one branded dashboard. Natively, those live in four separate places.

A typical build includes:

  • A Next.js / React frontend hosted on your own domain.
  • Live data via the GHL API, the Google Ads and Facebook Ads APIs, and the Stripe API.
  • Per-client secure login so each account sees only their data.
  • One-click PDF export for monthly reporting.

Timeline: 2-3 weeks. This is one of the most requested builds — currently in use by 3+ GHL Prime clients.

Custom Build 2 — Automated Lead Scoring Engine

This engine scores every new contact from 0 to 100 based on behaviour, source, and profile, then routes them automatically the moment they enter your CRM.

What GHL can't do: complex, real-time, multi-point scoring that updates as a contact interacts. Native workflow triggers handle simple logic, not weighted multi-signal models.

How it works:

  • A webhook fires on every new contact and calls a scoring function.
  • Scoring rules: +20 from paid ads, +15 if stated budget exceeds $1k, +5 per page visit, +10 if they replied within 5 minutes.
  • The final score is written back to a custom field in GHL.
  • GHL workflows route on it: 70+ goes to a high-priority queue, 40-69 to standard follow-up, under 40 into a long-term drip.

Timeline: 1 week.

Custom Build 3 — GHL + Stripe + Client Portal Integration

A self-service portal where your clients log in to view their campaigns, see their invoices, and pay — all in one place, all under your brand.

What GHL can't do: deliver a unified CRM-plus-billing client portal under your own brand. GHL handles the CRM; Stripe handles billing; nothing natively fuses them into one logged-in experience.

The build includes:

  • Secure login at clients.youragency.com.
  • GHL API integration for pipeline status, conversations, and campaign stats.
  • Stripe API for invoices, payment history, and a pay-now button.
  • A fully white-labeled interface end to end.

Timeline: 3-4 weeks. Agencies that deploy it report cutting client email back-and-forth by around 60%, because clients self-serve the answers they used to email for.

Custom Build 4 — Multi-Location GHL Dashboard for Franchise Clients

A single dashboard that reports across 10 to 50 sub-accounts at once — built for franchise and multi-location clients.

What GHL can't do: cross-sub-account reporting in one view. Each GHL sub-account is siloed by design; comparing them natively means logging in and out repeatedly.

The dashboard shows:

  • Total leads per week across all locations.
  • Conversion rate per location.
  • Best and worst performing locations at a glance.
  • Pipeline value broken down by location.
  • A scheduled weekly email digest to leadership.

Timeline: 2-3 weeks.

Custom Build 5 — AI-Powered Follow-Up Writer

When a contact goes cold, this tool automatically generates a personalised follow-up message using AI drawn from the contact's actual conversation history, then queues it for human approval before anything sends.

What GHL can't do: use full conversation history as context to generate tailored messages at scale. Conversation AI replies in real time but does not author proactive, history-aware follow-ups across your whole list.

How it works:

  • A webhook fires when last activity exceeds 7 days.
  • The system pulls the contact's conversation history from the GHL API.
  • A Claude or OpenAI prompt writes a short, natural follow-up SMS that references prior context.
  • The draft is posted to Slack for approval.
  • On approval, it sends through the GHL API.

Timeline: 1 week.

How to Commission a Custom GHL Build

To scope a project accurately, GHL Prime needs answers to four questions:

  1. What problem are you solving? Is it about data you can't see, users who can't self-serve, or a decision you can't make fast enough?
  2. What data sources are involved? GHL alone, or GHL plus Stripe, Google Ads, Facebook Ads, or another tool?
  3. Who uses it? Your internal team, your clients, or both?
  4. What does success look like? Define the concrete outcome — hours saved, fewer emails, faster routing, clearer reporting.

With those four answers, GHL Prime can scope the work, give you an estimate, and start in under 48 hours.

blogPosts.title: How to Share Courses in GoHighLevel (Snapshot, Import & Export)
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn how to share courses in GoHighLevel using Snapshots, the Course Creator share link, and content import – plus the gotchas to re-check after every transfer.
blogPosts.content:
You’ve built a great course inside GoHighLevel and now you need it somewhere else — a client’s sub-account, a fresh location, or a template you can reuse across your agency. The good news is that you don’t have to rebuild it lesson by lesson. The catch is that there are several ways to move a course, each with its own quirks, and picking the wrong one costs you hours of cleanup.

This guide walks through how to share courses GoHighLevel offers natively — via Snapshot, via the Course Creator share link, and via content import — and exactly what to re-check after every transfer so your students never see a broken lesson.

The three ways to share a GoHighLevel course

Before you touch anything, it helps to know which method fits your goal. GoHighLevel gives you three practical routes for course transfer in GHL, and they don’t all move the same things:

  • Snapshot: Best when you want to clone an entire setup — the course plus its offers, workflows, and related assets — into another sub-account at once.
  • Course Creator share/clone link: Best when you only need the course content itself moved into an existing location quickly.
  • Import from another course: Best when you’re merging or copying lessons and modules within the same agency or between two locations you control.

Each is covered step by step below.

Method 1: Share a course with a Snapshot

A Snapshot is GoHighLevel’s way of packaging up a sub-account — or selected assets from it — so you can load that configuration into another location. Membership products (your courses) can be included, which makes Snapshots the cleanest option when you want everything to travel together.

Steps

  • Create the Snapshot from your agency view: go to Settings > Snapshots, create a new Snapshot from the source sub-account, and confirm that Memberships/Courses are included in the assets.
  • Load it into the destination by pushing the Snapshot to an existing sub-account or using it to spin up a new one.
  • Open the destination Memberships area and confirm the course, its modules, and lessons came through.

Because GoHighLevel moved heavy membership processing to dedicated workers, Snapshot loads that include courses are more reliable than they used to be — but a course-heavy Snapshot can still take a few minutes to finish. Don’t panic if everything isn’t visible the instant the load completes; give it time, then verify.

Method 2: Use the Course Creator share / clone link

If you only need the course content in another location — not the whole sub-account — the share link is faster. This is the method most people mean when they ask how to share GoHighLevel course content directly between accounts.

Steps

  • In the source account, open Memberships > Courses, select the course, and use the share/clone option to generate an import link.
  • In the destination account, use the import option in the Courses area and paste the link, or use the Import from another course feature to pull the structure in.
  • Choose what to import — you can typically bring across full modules and lessons rather than rebuilding them.

This route copies the course skeleton and content references, which is exactly what you want when the destination already has its own branding, domain, and offers set up.

Method 3: Export and import course content (and the gotchas)

Whether you use a Snapshot or a share link, the structure usually arrives intact — but the structure is not the whole course. Several things commonly need a manual pass after any GoHighLevel membership sharing operation. Skip this and your students hit dead ends.

  • Videos and files: Hosted video and downloadable file references can break or point back to the original account. Open each lesson and confirm the media actually plays and downloads in the new location.
  • Drip settings: Drip schedules (lessons released X days after enrollment) don’t always carry over cleanly. Re-check every module’s drip configuration so content unlocks on the right timeline.
  • Offers and pricing: Offers, products, and price points usually need to be re-created or re-linked in the destination account, because billing is tied to that location’s payment integration. Don’t assume a paid course is still gated — test the checkout.
  • Enrollment automations: Workflows that grant course access on payment or tag often need their actions re-pointed to the new course in the new account.

This is where most DIY transfers go wrong: the lessons look fine in the dashboard, but the offer is missing, the drip is off, or a video silently fails. A 10-minute checklist saves a support ticket avalanche.

White-label course delivery for clients

If you’re delivering courses to clients, the point isn’t just moving content — it’s making the course feel like their product. GoHighLevel lets you serve the membership area under your client’s brand and custom domain, so students log in to a learning portal that looks fully owned by the business, not by GoHighLevel and not by you.

  • Custom domain: Point the membership/course portal at the client’s own domain or subdomain.
  • Branding: Apply the client’s logo, colors, and naming so nothing reveals the underlying platform.
  • Clean handoff: Combine white-label delivery with a Snapshot so each new client gets a consistent, branded course experience from day one.

This is exactly the kind of work our team handles routinely — and because we hold the GoHighLevel Course Creator certification, we know which assets travel with a course and which ones silently don’t. That certification is the difference between a transfer that “mostly works” and one your client never has to think about.

When to share vs. when to rebuild

Sharing isn’t always the right call. Use this rule of thumb:

  • Share when the course is stable, you want an exact copy, and you’re moving between accounts you control or onto a clean client sub-account.
  • Rebuild when the original was messy, the structure is changing anyway, or you’re consolidating several old courses — importing broken setups just carries the mess with you.

If you’re unsure, a quick audit usually answers it: count how many offers, drip rules, and automations are wired into the original. The more there are, the more a Snapshot saves you — and the more a careless import can break.

FAQ

Do products and offers transfer with the course?

Not reliably. Course structure (modules and lessons) transfers well, but offers, products, and pricing are tied to the destination account’s payment setup and usually need to be re-created or re-linked. Always test the checkout after transferring.

Do student enrollments transfer?

No. Existing learner enrollments and progress stay with the original account — sharing a course moves the content, not the people enrolled in it. In the new account you’ll grant access via offers or enrollment workflows. Plan a migration path for active students separately.

Will drip schedules and videos come across?

The settings often come across, but they need verification. Re-check drip timing on every module and confirm each video and downloadable file actually loads in the destination before you announce the course.

Get your courses moved cleanly

Sharing a GoHighLevel course is straightforward in theory and full of small traps in practice — broken video links, missing offers, drip schedules that quietly reset. If you’d rather have it done right the first time, our certified team handles the Snapshot, the import, the white-label setup, and the post-transfer checklist for you. blogPosts.title: GHL Voice AI: When the Human Transfer Doesn’t Pick Up
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: With GHL Voice AI, what happens when a call transfer fails because the client doesn’t pick up? Here’s how to build a graceful fallback into SMS and WhatsApp.
blogPosts.content:
You set up your GoHighLevel Voice AI agent to answer inbound calls, qualify the caller, and warm-transfer the hot ones to a human. It works beautifully—until the human doesn’t pick up. The phone rings out, the caller is left hanging, and a perfectly good lead evaporates. So the very specific question is this: with GHL Voice AI, when the AI transfers a call and the client (or your team) doesn’t answer, what actually happens, and how do you make the AI recover gracefully?

The short answer: yes, this is absolutely achievable with the right workflow design. The transfer doesn’t have to be a dead end. You can have the AI take the call back, capture a voicemail, route to a backup AI agent, and—most importantly—drop the caller into an SMS or WhatsApp follow-up so the lead is never lost. Here’s how the pieces fit together.

Call Transfer vs. Agent Transfer: know the difference first

Before you can design a fallback, you need to understand the two kinds of transfer GHL Voice AI supports, because they fail differently.

  • Call Transfer hands the live call to a human at a phone number. This is your warm or cold transfer to a salesperson, a receptionist, or the business owner. This is the one that can “fail”—because a human might not answer.
  • Agent Transfer hands the call to another AI agent, with no phone number involved. The caller stays in a single continuous conversation as they move from, say, a qualifying agent to a booking-focused agent or a support agent. An Agent Transfer doesn’t “ring out” the way a human transfer does.

The unanswered-transfer problem is specific to Call Transfer. When the human number doesn’t pick up, you need a plan for where the call goes next—and that plan is what separates a polished system from a frustrating one.

What happens when the human doesn’t pick up

By default, an unanswered Call Transfer needs somewhere to land, or the caller is simply dropped. GHL gives you a fallback sequence you configure on the agent and the connected phone number. The practical options, in the order most teams use them:

  • Hand the call back to the AI. Instead of ending the call, route it back to the Voice AI agent so it can apologise smoothly, offer to take a message, or book a callback. The caller never hits silence.
  • Drop to voicemail capture. Let the AI collect the reason for the call and the best number, or route to a voicemail box, so nothing is lost even if no one is available.
  • Use an AI agent as backup. GHL has an “AI Agent as a backup to the number / number pool” concept—the AI steps in when a human-first route goes unanswered. You can apply the same thinking in reverse: human first, AI as the safety net behind the transfer.

The move that saves the lead: route a failed transfer into SMS and WhatsApp

This is the part most people miss. A voicemail is fine, but the highest-converting recovery is to immediately follow up by text. Because every Voice AI call produces post-call outputs—a summary, a transcript, and extracted data—and because post-call workflows fire for the root agent and any agent in the transfer chain, you can detect a failed transfer and react automatically.

Here’s the recovery flow we build for clients:

  • Capture the number. The AI already has the caller’s phone number (and often a name and intent) from the conversation. That data lands on the contact record.
  • Trigger a workflow on the post-call event. Use the call outcome—transfer attempted but not connected—as the branch condition in a GHL workflow.
  • Send an SMS immediately. Something like: “Hi {{contact.first_name}}, sorry we missed you just now—this is [Business]. Want me to book a quick call?” Speed matters; the first few minutes after a missed connection convert best.
  • Add a WhatsApp branch. If the contact is reachable on WhatsApp (now natively supported in GHL), send the same message there. Many people answer WhatsApp faster than SMS.
  • Offer a booking link or a callback. Include a calendar link, or use the Smart Callback feature so the AI re-dials at a time the lead chooses. The lead picks the slot; you stop playing phone tag.

Done well, the caller hangs up from an unanswered transfer and—within seconds—gets a friendly text offering to reschedule. That’s the difference between a lost call and a booked appointment.

Use working hours so after-hours calls route differently

Half of “the human didn’t answer” is really “the human wasn’t working.” Configure your agent’s business hours so the transfer logic changes by time of day:

  • During hours: attempt the Call Transfer to a human, with the AI and SMS/WhatsApp follow-up as backups.
  • After hours: skip the human transfer entirely. Let the AI handle the conversation end to end, capture details, book straight into the calendar, and queue a follow-up message for the morning.

This single change removes most of your dead-air transfers, because the system never tries to ring a human who has gone home.

A simple blueprint for a graceful fallback

  • 1. AI answers, follows its prompt, and qualifies the caller.
  • 2. If qualified and within business hours, attempt a Call Transfer to the human.
  • 3. If the human doesn’t answer, hand the call back to the AI (or a backup AI agent) to take a message and offer a callback.
  • 4. On call end, a post-call workflow checks the outcome.
  • 5. If the transfer failed, fire SMS plus WhatsApp follow-up and offer a booking link or Smart Callback.
  • 6. After hours, the AI handles everything and queues a next-morning follow-up.

FAQ

Does the call just drop if no one answers the transfer?

Only if you haven’t set a fallback. Configure the AI to take the call back or route to voicemail so the caller always lands somewhere.

Can the AI follow up by text automatically?

Yes. Because every call produces post-call data and fires workflows, you can trigger an SMS and/or WhatsApp message the moment a transfer fails—no manual step.

What’s the difference between Agent Transfer and Call Transfer again?

Call Transfer goes to a human at a phone number; Agent Transfer hands off to another AI agent. Only the human transfer can “ring out,” which is why it needs a fallback.

Can it book the callback for me?

Yes—use a calendar link in the follow-up message or the Smart Callback feature so the AI re-dials at the lead’s chosen time.

Build it once, never lose a transfer again

An unanswered transfer should feel invisible to the caller and impossible to lose for you. That takes deliberate design: the right transfer type, a clean fallback, business-hours logic, and a post-call SMS and WhatsApp workflow that catches every dropped connection. We design exactly these fallback flows as part of our AI agent builder service—built, tested, and tuned to your call volume. If your Voice AI is leaking leads on failed transfers, contact us and we’ll map the recovery flow for you.

blogPosts.title: Stripe Rebilling in GHL SaaS Mode: The Reseller Setup Guide
blogPosts.author: GHL Prime Team
blogPosts.excerpt: A reseller-focused guide to GoHighLevel SaaS Mode rebilling subscriptions with Stripe: connect your account, set markup multipliers, and keep every subscriber profitable.
blogPosts.content:
If you are reselling GoHighLevel under your own brand, your monthly subscription price is only half the equation. The other half is usage — the SMS, voice minutes, emails, and AI your subscribers burn through every day. Rebilling is the mechanism that recovers those costs and turns them into margin instead of a line item that quietly eats your profit. Done right, every subscriber pays for what they use and a little extra on top. Done wrong, you are subsidizing your own clients.

This guide is a focused walkthrough of GoHighLevel SaaS Mode rebilling subscriptions with Stripe — the prerequisites, the wallet model, how to set markup multipliers that keep accounts profitable, and the failures that catch most resellers off guard. It assumes you already understand the basics of SaaS Mode and want to get the billing side genuinely right.

Prerequisites: What You Need Before Rebilling Works

Rebilling is not a standalone feature you toggle on. It is gated behind SaaS Mode, which has two hard requirements:

  • The Agency Pro plan at $497/mo. Rebilling with agency markup is only available on this tier. The $97 Starter and $297 Unlimited plans do not unlock it. If you are on a lower plan, this is your first upgrade.
  • A connected agency Stripe account. Stripe is the only payment provider SaaS Mode supports. Your agency Stripe account is what collects subscription payments and, critically, what charges client cards to top up their usage wallets. No connected Stripe means no rebilling — full stop.

Connect Stripe from your agency settings under the Payments or SaaS configuration area. Use a fully verified, live Stripe account — not test mode — and confirm payouts are enabled. A half-configured Stripe account is the single most common reason rebilling silently fails to charge anyone.

How Rebilling Actually Works: The Wallet Model

The mental model that trips up new resellers is assuming usage is billed like a phone bill — tallied up and charged at the end of the month. It is not. GoHighLevel rebilling runs on a prepaid wallet with auto-recharge.

Here is the flow. Each sub-account has its own wallet. When a subscriber uses a billable service — sends an SMS, makes a call, sends a batch of emails, runs an AI action — the cost (plus your markup) is deducted from that wallet in real time. When the wallet balance drops below a threshold you set, GoHighLevel automatically charges the client’s saved card via your Stripe account to recharge it back up.

So there are two numbers that matter for auto-recharge:

  • The trigger threshold — “when balance is lower than” a set amount.
  • The recharge amount — how much to add back when that threshold is hit.

For example, you might recharge with $20 whenever the wallet drops below $10. The client never sees an invoice for individual messages; they just see periodic top-ups on their card, and services keep running uninterrupted. Your job as the reseller is to make sure those top-ups always cost the client more than they cost you.

Configuring Markup Multipliers

The markup multiplier is where your margin lives. GoHighLevel charges you a base cost for each usage type (phone numbers, voice minutes, SMS/MMS, email, AI, premium workflow actions). The multiplier you set determines what the client’s wallet is charged for that same usage.

The math is straightforward. If your SMS cost is $0.01 per message and you set a 3x multiplier, the client’s wallet is charged $0.03. You keep $0.02. If a client sends 100 messages that cost you $10 and your multiplier is 5x, their wallet is charged $50 and you net $40.

By default, GoHighLevel sets a 1.05x markup — a 5% bump that exists only to cover Stripe’s processing fees on the recharge. 1.05x is not a profit margin. If you leave the default in place, you are barely breaking even after Stripe takes its cut. You need to set a multiplier on each of these deliberately:

  • Phone & voice minutes — inbound/outbound call minutes and number rental. Voice-heavy clients (especially anyone running AI voice agents) can move real volume here, so do not underprice it.
  • SMS & MMS — usually the highest-volume service. Even a small per-message markup compounds fast.
  • Email — cheap per message but sent in bulk, so the multiplier still matters at scale.
  • AI usage — conversational AI, content actions, and AI voice consume credits quickly. Mark these up confidently; AI is a premium feature and clients expect to pay for it.

You can set these per sub-account in the account settings, or standardize them across many accounts at once using the SaaS Configurator and bulk rebilling tools. For a growing reseller, configure your defaults once in the Configurator so every new sub-account inherits a profitable markup automatically rather than launching at 1.05x.

Setting Markup So Every Subscriber Is Profitable

A practical rule: pick a multiplier high enough that a light-usage client still contributes margin, and a heavy-usage client funds your overhead. Many resellers land in the 2x–5x range depending on the service. Lower for commodity SMS/email if you are price-sensitive in a competitive niche; higher for AI and voice where perceived value is high. Whatever you choose, model your worst case — your heaviest user on your thinnest markup — and confirm you are still profitable there. If that account loses money, your markup is too low.

Common Rebilling Failures and How to Fix Them

Most rebilling problems are not bugs — they are configuration gaps. These are the ones we see repeatedly.

  • Stripe not connected (or in test mode). Nothing charges, wallets never recharge, and services may stop the moment trial credits run out. Fix: reconnect a fully verified live Stripe account and confirm it is the one bound to SaaS Mode.
  • Client card declined or wallet empty. When auto-recharge fails — expired card, insufficient funds — the wallet drains to zero and usage-based services pause. Fix: enable dunning-style retries where available, prompt clients to update payment methods, and set the recharge threshold high enough that a single decline does not instantly halt service.
  • Services pausing when the balance hits zero. This is by design, not a malfunction — a zero wallet stops SMS, calls, and AI. The fix is preventative: set a sensible recharge trigger and amount so the balance is topped up well before it bottoms out.
  • Markup set too low. The quiet killer. At 1.05x you may technically “rebill” while netting nothing after Stripe fees. Fix: raise multipliers across SMS, email, voice, and AI to real margins and apply them in bulk.
  • Premium triggers and actions not billing. Some premium workflow actions and integrations have their own usage costs that need rebilling enabled and a multiplier set. If you overlooked them, you eat the cost. Fix: audit your premium actions and confirm each billable one has a markup configured.

Handling Refunds and Chargebacks

Because recharges run through your agency Stripe account, refunds and chargebacks land on you, not on GoHighLevel. If a client disputes a wallet top-up, Stripe pulls the funds plus a dispute fee from your account. Keep clear records of what each recharge paid for — usage logs in the sub-account are your evidence. For goodwill refunds, issue them from Stripe and adjust the wallet credit manually if needed so the books stay consistent. The best defense against chargebacks is transparency: tell clients up front, in plain language, that usage is prepaid and auto-recharged, so a top-up on their statement is never a surprise.

FAQ

Do I need Stripe specifically, or can I use another processor?

Stripe is the only payment provider SaaS Mode supports for rebilling. Other processors will not drive the wallet recharge mechanism.

Is rebilling available on the $297 plan?

No. Rebilling with markup requires the Agency Pro $497/mo plan, which is what unlocks SaaS Mode in full.

What happens to my margin if a client barely uses the platform?

Low usage means low rebilling revenue, but your fixed monthly subscription price still covers you. Rebilling is upside on top of the base plan, not a replacement for pricing your subscription correctly.

Can I change a client’s markup after they sign up?

Yes. Markup multipliers can be adjusted per sub-account or in bulk at any time, and changes apply to future usage.

The implementation of the "Brainy" assistant has transformed BrainyBox's Messenger channel from a simple communication line into a powerful automated commerce engine. The image-to-SKU feature provides a unique and highly effective way for customers to shop. The end-to-end order automation has eliminated manual data entry, reduced errors, and allows the sales team to focus on growth while the bot handles the transactional dialogue.

caseStudies.title: Automated PDF Application Generation
caseStudies.subtitle: Automating the conversion of raw web form data into a professionally formatted, branded, and distributed PDF application document.
caseStudies.challenge: Veritas Pathways collected detailed student application data through online forms. The subsequent process of converting this raw data into a standardized, professionally branded PDF document for internal records was a manual, time-consuming task. This created a significant bottleneck in the application pipeline, was susceptible to human error during data transfer, and resulted in inconsistent document formatting.
caseStudies.solution: An end-to-end automated workflow was designed in n8n. The process begins with a webhook that instantly captures the student's application data upon submission. A Code node then cleans, formats, and structures the data. This prepared data is passed to a second Code node, which dynamically generates a complete HTML document, injecting the applicant's information into a styled template with custom CSS for branding. The workflow then uses a dedicated node to send this HTML to a service that converts it into a PDF, downloads the finished file, and emails it as an attachment to the admissions team for immediate processing.
caseStudies.outcome: The automation completely eliminated the manual effort required to create and dispatch application documents. Veritas Pathways now has a robust system that instantly generates a consistent, professionally branded PDF for every application submitted. This has dramatically accelerated their internal processing times, eliminated formatting errors, and ensures that every student's record is presented in a uniform and official manner, significantly boosting administrative efficiency.
caseStudies.excerpt: This case study outlines an automated workflow created for Veritas Pathways. The system captures student application data from a webhook, dynamically generates a professionally styled HTML document, converts it into a high-quality PDF, and automatically emails the final document to the admissions team. This automation eliminates manual work, ensuring speed, accuracy, and brand consistency.
body: Veritas Pathways faced a significant operational bottleneck in their admissions process. While data collection was efficient via online forms, the crucial step of creating an official, branded PDF from that data was entirely manual. This repetitive task consumed valuable administrative time, introduced the risk of data entry errors, and made it difficult to maintain a consistent, professional look across all application documents.

The implemented solution is a linear, event-driven n8n workflow. It is triggered by a webhook that receives the raw application data. The workflow then executes a series of automated steps: it first parses and formats the incoming data, then dynamically constructs a complete HTML document using a predefined template with CSS for styling. This HTML is sent to an external API to be converted into a PDF, which is then downloaded and emailed as an attachment to the relevant department.

The impact on efficiency was immediate and substantial. The entire document generation process is now instantaneous, running 24/7 without any human intervention. The admissions team receives a perfectly formatted, professional PDF the moment a student applies, allowing them to focus on reviewing applicants rather than on administrative tasks. This has streamlined their entire workflow, reduced errors, and ensured a high standard of presentation for all official records.

caseStudies.title: Stateless AI Assistant for Real-Time Internal Operations
caseStudies.subtitle: Developing a secure, tool-based AI agent that interacts with live company APIs for employee and task management, ensuring data accuracy and integrity.
caseStudies.challenge: A system was needed to allow employees to query internal company data and manage daily tasks using natural language. The primary challenges were ensuring the AI always provided up-to-the-minute information, preventing it from acting on stale or cached data, and guaranteeing absolute data integrity, especially when creating new tasks with specific user assignments.
caseStudies.solution: An n8n workflow was built around an AI agent with a strictly defined "stateless" directive: it has no memory and must call a live data tool for every user request. The agent is equipped with a suite of HTTP request tools, each corresponding to a specific API endpoint for actions like retrieving employee details or fetching tasks. For task creation, a mandatory, multi-step process was enforced: the AI must first use lookup tools to resolve all employee names or emails into their unique database _ids before it is permitted to call the task creation tool.
caseStudies.outcome: The solution provides a powerful and safe conversational interface for internal operations. The "stateless" rule guarantees that all responses reflect the real-time status of the company's data. The rigid ID-resolution protocol for creating tasks eliminates the risk of data corruption or incorrect assignments. This allows employees to efficiently query information and manage tasks through a simple chat interface, boosting productivity while maintaining strict data governance.
caseStudies.excerpt: This case study details a stateless AI assistant built for internal company operations. By forcing the AI to use live data tools for every query and enforcing a strict ID-resolution protocol before creating new tasks, the system provides an accurate, secure, and highly efficient way for employees to interact with company data through a natural language interface.
body: The primary challenge was to create a conversational AI that could serve as a central hub for internal company data, such as employee directories and daily tasks. This posed two significant risks: the AI could provide outdated information from its memory, and it could corrupt the database by creating records with ambiguous inputs like names instead of unique, immutable identifiers.

The solution is an AI agent built within an n8n workflow, governed by a critical system prompt that makes it entirely "stateless"—it must re-fetch data using a specific tool for every single user query. For creating new tasks, the AI is forced through a strict, multi-step validation: it must first call employee lookup tools to retrieve the unique database _id for both the manager and all assignees before it can proceed with the creation request.

This architecture resulted in a highly reliable and secure internal assistant. Data accuracy is guaranteed because every response is based on a live API call. The rigid validation process for creating new records ensures database integrity. Employees now have a powerful, single point of contact to get real-time information and delegate tasks, dramatically improving operational efficiency.

caseStudies.title: AI-Powered Customer Support with Dynamic User Verification
caseStudies.subtitle: Implementing a context-aware AI agent to streamline customer interactions and securely manage user data for OptimalMD.
caseStudies.challenge: OptimalMD required a 24/7 customer support solution capable of handling diverse user queries. The primary challenge was to differentiate between unauthenticated guests and verified customers, providing general information to the former while securely offering personalized, account-specific support to the latter, and escalating issues efficiently when necessary.
caseStudies.solution: An automated workflow was built around a central AI Agent. The system uses distinct operational modes: a "Guest Mode" for general inquiries and a "Verified Mode" for authenticated users. A secure OTP (One-Time Password) system, triggered by dedicated webhooks, manages the transition between modes. In Verified Mode, the AI is granted tool access to perform actions like fetching user data from a CRM via an HTTP request and creating support tickets through a dedicated API.
caseStudies.outcome: The solution provides an intelligent, secure, and scalable customer support channel. It effectively enhances security by restricting data access until a user is verified. It improves operational efficiency by automating routine queries and ticket creation, freeing up the human support team. This results in a superior, always-on user experience where customers receive instant, context-appropriate assistance.
caseStudies.excerpt: This case study details the creation of an automated AI support agent for OptimalMD. The solution features a dual-mode system (Guest vs. Verified) with secure OTP authentication, enabling the AI to provide general information to all visitors while offering personalized, data-driven support and automated actions for authenticated users, significantly improving efficiency and security.
body: OptimalMD faced the common challenge of providing scalable, 24/7 customer support while adhering to strict data privacy requirements. They needed a system that could intelligently distinguish between prospective customers asking general questions and existing members needing account-specific help, without compromising security.

We implemented a sophisticated workflow powered by an AI Agent that uses a secure OTP verification process to switch between two operational modes. In 'Guest Mode,' the AI acts as an informational guide. Upon successful verification, it transitions to 'Verified Mode,' unlocking tools to automatically fetch user profiles from a CRM and create support tickets via API calls.

The new automated system provides an immediate, secure, and context-aware support experience. It successfully segregates user interactions, safeguarding private data while empowering verified users with self-service capabilities. This has significantly improved support efficiency and provided a scalable solution for OptimalMD's growing customer base.

caseStudies.title: GoHighLevel and CINC Ai Agent Integration
caseStudies.subtitle: GoHighLevel AI outbound call setup for Real-estate
caseStudies.challenge:
Built a custom GoHighLevel CRM automation system for real estate lead management.

Leads from CINC and other real estate CRMs are pushed into GHL via Zapier. Once the lead is created, GHL triggers a webhook to a SimpleTalk Voice AI agent, which automatically calls the prospect for qualification and follow-up.

Call results (status, intent, notes) are sent back to GoHighLevel, where the system updates pipeline stages and triggers the next workflow based on the conversation outcome.

This setup removes manual follow-up, ensures immediate contact, and keeps the CRM fully synchronized.
